question: What will Chhattisgarh's cumulative confirmed 2026 H1N1 (swine flu) case count reach in state Health Department data reported on or after September 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Base: 205 cumulative as of the Sep 5 Health Department release, with a ~9-day doubling time over Aug 27-Sep 5 and daily new cases trending up (15 on Sep 3, 26 on Sep 5). A Sep 17 report will most likely quote data through ~Sep 15-16, i.e. ~11 days of further accumulation. Straight continuation of the observed 9-day doubling gives ~478; deceleration to a 14-day doubling gives ~355; mild acceleration toward the Dehradun district pattern (4.3-day doubling, still 28/day at 328 cumulative) gives 600+. Mid-September is still inside India's Aug-Oct influenza season, spread has reached all 33 districts, testing is expanding, and an Ambikapur jail cluster (100+ symptomatic inmates) is a plausible step-jump; those push the right tail. Offsetting: cumulative growth rates always decay, the wave is maturing, and the resolving figure may be a stale or lower-variant number given that outlets already disagree by ~15-20 on the same date. Median 470. Upside escape priced at 10% (a Dehradun-style ~6-day doubling clears 750); downside escape at 4% (needs a collapse from 26/day to ~4/day, or the resolving report quoting a materially stale total).

calls.reasoning: Prior from a named class: Chhattisgarh's own mid-September H1N1 cumulative in its last comparable outbreak year - 288 on Sep 17, 2022, from 203 on Sep 3, 2022 (+85/14 days). 2026 sits at 205 on Sep 4, an almost identical level and date, so 288 is the anchor before news. Two adjustments push well above it. First, 2026's wave is steeply accelerating where 2022's was flat: increments ran +10, +15, +22, +24, +29 over Aug 31-Sep 4, versus ~4/day in 2022. Second, 2026 is a far larger national influenza year (Delhi ~2,300 cases by late Aug vs 229 in the same 2025 period; ICMR calls it seasonal, H1N1pdm09, ~98% of Influenza A), and Chhattisgarh's wave began late (late August), so Sep 5-16 likely spans the peak rather than the tail. Twelve days from 205 at an average 12-45/day spans ~350-745; a 2.0-2.5x 12-day multiplier, typical of an actively surging state count, gives 410-510. I discount straight-line extrapolation of +29/day because these are testing- and attention-driven confirmed counts that historically burn out within 1-2 weeks of the media peak (which was Sep 4-5's '200 crossed' cycle), and because the Aug 27-Sep 4 average was only 12.5/day. Median 480 (~23/day). Counterargument for lower: lab capacity caps confirmations, and the first report dated Sep 17 may cite data several days stale. Counterargument for higher: all districts now reporting, Raipur alone at 89 and adding 12/day, and testing expansion under CMHO directives could step the series up. Escapes: 7% above 750 (sustained ~45/day plus a testing ramp); 3% below 250 (wave stops dead or the qualifying report quotes a materially older/narrower figure). No market exists on this. Evidence is thin on Sep 5-7 - nothing indexed past the Sep 4 data - so I stay nearer the reference class than a naive extrapolation would put me.
